title: Three Ways to Make Stone
question: How do the three main kinds of rock form?
hook: Every rock you pick up got its start in one of three very different ways.
idea: Rocks are grouped by how they form: cooled magma or lava makes igneous rock, hardened sediment makes sedimentary rock, and heat and pressure remake existing rock into metamorphic rock.

beats.prompt: Sort each way of forming rock into the group it makes
items: Magma cools slowly inside the crust
Weathered grains are deposited and harden
Older rock is heated and squeezed without melting
beats.explain: Igneous rock comes from cooling magma or lava, sedimentary rock from hardened sediment, and metamorphic rock from existing rock transformed by high pressure and temperature.

beats.prompt: A body of magma stays trapped deep inside the crust and cools and crystallizes very slowly. What kind of rock results?

choices.label: A volcanic rock such as pumice
choices.feedback: Volcanic rocks form only when magma reaches the surface as lava or ejecta.

choices.label: A sedimentary rock such as sandstone
choices.feedback: Sedimentary rock needs weathered grains to be laid down and hardened, not cooling magma.

choices.label: A plutonic rock such as granite
A metamorphic rock remade by pressure
choices.feedback: Metamorphic rock comes from existing rock changed without melting, not from magma cooling.

beats.explain: Magma that cools and crystallizes slowly within the crust forms plutonic, or intrusive, rock, and granite is a common example.

beats.prompt: Put the steps that lead to sedimentary rock in order
items: The sediment is lithified into rock
beats.explain: Weathering, transport and deposition of existing rock make sediment, and lithification of that sediment then forms sedimentary rock.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Igneous rock forms when magma or lava cools and hardens.
That magma comes from partly melted older rock in the mantle or crust.
Rock can only melt if its temperature goes up.
So every igneous rock traces back to rock that was heated.
beats.explain: Rock can also melt when the pressure on it drops or its composition changes, not only when its temperature rises.
